clinician.final_diagnosis: Primary Cardiac Lymphoma (DLBCL) with cerebral relapse in 2012
clinician.trajectory_summary: In 2007, a 37-year-old Hispanic man presented with hemodynamic cardiac compromise. Cardiac MRI revealed an 8.4×7.4×7.6 cm mass invading the right atrium and mediastinum. Biopsy diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). FDG-PET imaging showed no pathological uptake in the brain, head/neck, or cervical lymph nodes, and subsequent total-body imaging surveillance (2007-2011) confirmed no extracardiac disease, establishing Primary Cardiac Lymphoma. The patient completed 8 cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy and involved field radiotherapy. Approximately one month post-radiation, mediastinal recurrence was detected, prompting salvage therapy with 2 cycles of R-ESHAP followed by high-dose BEAM chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation. The patient remained in complete remission for 4 years per serial total-body FDG-PET, CT, and MRI surveillance. In 2012, he presented with a 3-month history of progressive memory deficits, severe daytime sleepiness, and behavioral changes (apathy, hyperphagia). Brain imaging demonstrated a 21×26×25 mm uniformly enhancing mass in the third ventricle involving the hypothalamus with suprasellar extension. Brain biopsy confirmed recurrent DLBCL with flow cytometric immunophenotyping showing monoclonal B-cells positive for CD10, CD19, and CD20 with kappa light chain restriction. The immunophenotype was documented as similar to the original cardiac tumor, confirming cerebral relapse of the primary cardiac lymphoma.
